labels.label: def:almost_trivial_loop

hypotheses.paper: U open, x in closure U

findings: l.1201 calls 'same connected component of the compact-open Omega(x,y,U)' and 'homotopic with respect to U' equivalent; only homotopic => same component holds in general (proved, GX.OmegaHomotopic.mem_connectedComponentIn); the converse needs Omega(x,y,U) locally path-connected, which the hypotheses do not give when x, y lie on the frontier of U
questions: Reading (a): 'connected component' read as homotopy with respect to U (the paper's 'or, equivalently', l.1201); the literal compact-open form GX.AlmostTrivialCC is defined and implied. Ruling wanted before marking this and the six labels built on it.

labels.label: ex:consider_carthesian_coordinates_usual

sorries.obstruction: pi_1 of R^3 minus the closed topologist's sine curve with its limit segment: needs a deformation of the complement of an epsilon-neighbourhood of S2 onto R^3 minus a line (the homeomorphism asserted at l.1227) and a limit over epsilon; the paper leaves it to the reader

the paper's proof (l.1227) rests on 'Y minus closed B(S2,eps) is homeomorphic to Y minus S1' and pushes the middle of the loop into B minus B(S2,eps); needs an explicit isotopy of R^3 moving the eps-neighbourhood of the sine curve onto a neighbourhood of a segment, equivalently the surjectivity of pi_1(B(O,r) minus S2) -> pi_1(R^3 minus S2)

the proof uses mod 2 intersection numbers of loops with {z=0} and with the components ('pockets') of {z=0} minus S2 in a ball, and their homotopy invariance (MR2680546); neither intersection theory for continuous curves nor a substitute (a double cover of B minus S2 flipping across finitely many pockets, or a planar separation lemma on the homotopy square) is available

findings: l.1216: S2 is printed as {y = sin(1/x)} union a segment, which in R^3 is a surface (z free); read with z = 0 on the graph (the planar topologist's sine curve), as the proof's 'plane {z=0}' and claim 1 require
l.1243-1244: H'(s,t) = (0, lambda_s t, 0) lies on the segment of S2; with gamma(t) = (0,0,t) near the ends it should read (0, 0, lambda_s t) and (0, 0, -lambda_s t)
l.1218: 'The isomorphism is given by the number of turns around S_i' — for S1 this is GX.cartDeg (winding of y + iz), proved bijective
questions: Reading (g): 'homotopically trivial' (l.1219) read as a homotopy with fixed ends to the constant loop through loops of Omega(O,O,U), the constant loop reached only at the end (GX.IsHomTrivial), since the constant loop at O is not in Omega(O,O,Y minus S_i).

labels.label: ex:consider_fiber_above_homeomorphic

hypotheses.note: as C; S skeletal and C minus S slsc are proved, not assumed

findings: l.1414: 'the natural map pi_1(a,D_{n+1}) -> pi_1(a,D_n) has an infinite fiber above every point' is asserted without proof; it is supplied (paths gamma*omega*x_n^j*omega', x_n a small circle around 1/n, told apart by their winding around 1/n read through exp, invariant under free-end homotopy in D_{n+1})

l.1415: 'the result follows' also needs the sets pi_1(a,D_n) countable (proved: pi_1(C minus S) is countable and maps onto them) and pi_1(a,D_1) countable nonempty; the limit is pi_1(a,D_1) x N^N, homeomorphic to Z^N
l.1409: 'answers positively Problem 10.8 of MR2198590' is bibliographic and not formalized

kb_proposals: pi_1(C minus 0) = Z is in the scaffold (GX.cWinding, Branched/Paths): winding through Complex.isCoveringMap_exp, invariance by IsCoveringMap.liftPath_apply_one_eq_of_homotopicRel, injectivity by GX.lineHomotopy in C mapped by exp — reuse it for any 'number of turns' claim

A free-end homotopy invariant: lift (t,s) -> c - H(s,t) with IsCoveringMap.liftHomotopy (time first, A = I), then IsCoveringMap.const_of_comp on exp shows an integer-valued quantity is constant (GX.argLift_freeHomotopic)
Under `open unitInterval`, `σ` and `I` are notations: a local named σ or a binder named I fails with an unreadable 'invalid pattern variable' or 'unexpected token'
Projective limits of towers of countable discrete sets with countably infinite fibres: GX.towerHomeomorph (≃ₜ A 0 × ℕ^ℕ) and GX.prodNatPiHomeomorph (≃ₜ ℕ^ℕ)
